# Somanassajātaka (Ja 505)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Somanassajātaka* (Ja 505), rendered in English as "Prince Happiness" or "The Story of Prince Somanassa," is a canonical verse narrative in the Pali Jātaka collection [Francis 2002]. According to the narrative framework set at Jetavana, the Buddha told the story regarding Devadatta's plots to kill him, explaining to the monks that this was not the first occasion on which Devadatta had attempted his life [Strong 2009; Fausböll 1887]. The verse cycle begins with the incipit *Ko taṁ hiṁsati heṭheti* [Fausböll 1887]. The story of the past takes place in the realm of the Kurus at the city of Uttarapañcāla during the reign of King Reṇu [Fausböll 1887]. A fraudulent ascetic is reprimanded by the Bodhisatta, Prince Somanassa, for his improper behavior; in revenge, the ascetic lies to the king and attempts to have the prince executed, but Somanassa defends himself successfully against the charges [Anandajoti 2010]. In this conflict between father and son, the prince's mother takes the side of her son [Ohnuma 2012]. Somanassa subsequently relinquishes his royal inheritance to retire as an ascetic in the Himālayas, providing a classic canonical illustration of the Bodhisatta's perfection of renunciation (*nekkhamma-pāramī*) [Anandajoti 2010; War Yar Mein Da 2015]. In the identification of the birth, the Buddha reveals the deceitful ascetic to have been Devadatta, the mother Mahāmāyā, the ascetic Rakkhita Sāriputta, and Prince Somanassa the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1887].
